These chapters are simply an attempt to record the gist of some conversations and noonday thoughts, which have arisen from time to time in idle moments spent in a garden on the Cotswold Hills, where there are gathered together certain features unusual in Western pleasances.

arxiv-1809-03901.creator: Elisabeth Lex, Mario Wagner, Dominik Kowald
arxiv-1809-03901.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Elisabeth Lex, Mario Wagner, Dominik Kowald. Contemporary politics are often discussed on social media and thus, social media is an important information and news source ( Conover et al. Politicians and parties increasingly use social media to spread their ideas, to interact with voters and/or critics and to shape the political debate ( Hong and Kim 2016 ; Jungherr 2016 ) .

arxiv-1907-08019.title: Transforming graph states to Bell-pairs is NP-Complete
arxiv-1907-08019.creator: Axel Dahlberg Jonas Helsen Stephanie Wehner
arxiv-1907-08019.description: Abstract Critical to the construction of large scale quantum networks, i.e. a quantum internet, is the development of fast algorithms for managing entanglement present in the network. One fundamental building block for a quantum internet is the distribution of Bell pairs between distant nodes in the network.

arxiv-2012-14254.description: Abstract We study the sum classic network creation game introduced by Fabrikant et al. in which n n players conform a network buying links at individual price α \alpha . arxiv-2112-10400.description: Abstract In this work, we study a status update system with a source node sending timely information to the destination through a channel with random delay. We measure the timeliness of the information stored at the receiver via the Age of Information (AoI), the time elapsed since the freshest sample stored at the receiver is generated.

arxiv-2403-09526.title: Optimizing the Electrical Interface for Large-Scale Color-Center Quantum Processors
arxiv-2403-09526.creator: Luc Enthoven 1, 2, Masoud Babaie 1, 3, Fabio Sebastiano 1, 2
arxiv-2403-09526.description: Abstract Quantum processors based on color centers in diamond are promising candidates for future large-scale quantum computers thanks to their flexible optical interface, (relatively) high operating temperature, and high-fidelity operation. Similar to other quantum-computing platforms, the electrical interface required to control and read out such qubits may limit both the performance of the whole system and its scalability.

arxiv-2404-04144.title: Theory of ultrathin ferroelectrics: the case of CsGeBr 3
arxiv-2404-04144.creator: Ravi Kashikar, Arlies Valdespino, Charlton Ogg, Edvin Uppgard, S. Lisenkov, I. Ponomareva
arxiv-2404-04144.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Ravi Kashikar, Arlies Valdespino, Charlton Ogg, Edvin Uppgard, S. Lisenkov, I. Ponomareva. Ferroelectricity has recently been demonstrated in germanium-based inorganic halide perovskites. We use atomistic first-principles-based simulations to study ultra-thin CsGeBr 3 films with thicknesses of 4-18 nm and develop a theory for ferroelectric ultrathin films.

arxiv-2501-17629.title: A rigorous Turing test: a foundation for evaluating artificial general intelligence
arxiv-2501-17629.creator: Sharon Temtsin, Diane Proudfoot, David Kaber, Christoph Bartneck
arxiv-2501-17629.description: Abstract Several studies claim that large language models have passed the Turing Test and hence can “think”, yet none follow Turing’s original instructions precisely. Passing the test holds significance as evidence that a machine demonstrates human-like intelligence, and as a marker for artificial-general intelligence in commercial and legal domains.

arxiv-2508-11406.title: Open, Reproducible and Trustworthy Robot-Based Experiments with Virtual Labs and Digital-Twin-Based Execution Tracing
arxiv-2508-11406.creator: Benjamin Alt, Mareike Picklum, Sorin Arion, Franklin Kenghagho Kenfack, Michael Beetz
arxiv-2508-11406.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Benjamin Alt, Mareike Picklum, Sorin Arion, Franklin Kenghagho Kenfack, Michael Beetz. We envision a future in which autonomous robots conduct scientific experiments in ways that are not only precise and repeatable, but also open, trustworthy, and transparent.

arxiv-2510-24566.title: Toward a Physical Interpretation of Phase Field Models with Dynamic Boundary Conditions
arxiv-2510-24566.creator: Xiaobo Jing, Qi Wang
arxiv-2510-24566.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Xiaobo Jing, Qi Wang. In recent decades, considerable research has been devoted to partial differential equations (PDEs) with dynamic boundary conditions. However, the physical interpretation of the parameters involved often remains unclear, which in turn limits both theoretical analysis and numerical computation. For instance, the Robin boundary condition used in thermodynamically consistent models with dynamic boundary conditions has been misinterpreted as representing a chemical reaction, or has been generalized in an unjustified manner in numerous works.

pmc-11365642.title: Peripheral ulcerative keratitis secondary to tuberculosis: A case report and literature review
pmc-11365642.creator: Shuang Wang, Yajie Gong, Keke Huang, Jun Huang
pmc-11365642.description: Rationale:Compared with intraocular tuberculosis, ocular tuberculosis with ocular surface involvement is rare. Corneal involvement in ocular tuberculosis may include interstitial keratitis or peripheral ulcerative keratitis. We report a case of peripheral ulcerative keratitis directly caused by tuberculosis.Patient concerns:A 20-year-old man complained of vision loss and pain in the left eye that had lasted for 1 week.

pmc-11372398.title: Long-Term Structural Changes Observed on Gonioscopy and Anterior-Segment OCT Following Gonioscopy-Assisted Transluminal Trabeculotomy
pmc-11372398.creator: Nese Alagoz, Ihsan Cakir, Cigdem Altan, Ercument Bozkurt, Zeynep Ipekli, Erdem Erdogdu, Tekin Yasar
pmc-11372398.description: Objectives:To evaluate the long-term structural changes of the anterior chamber (AC) angle following gonioscopy-assisted transluminal trabeculotomy (GATT).Methods:The AC angle of 10 eyes that underwent GATT at least 6 years previously was assessed for structural changes. A detailed gonioscopy was performed to determine the state of the cleft and the position of the trabecular flap.

pmc-11461197.title: GSTT1/GSTM1 deficiency aggravated cisplatin-induced acute kidney injury via ROS-triggered ferroptosis
pmc-11461197.creator: Peipei Li, Duopin Li, Yanfang Lu, Shaokang Pan, Fei Cheng, Shen Li, Xiaonan Zhang, Jinling Huo, Dongwei Liu, Zhangsuo Liu
pmc-11461197.description: IntroductionCisplatin is a widely used chemotherapeutic agent prescribed to treat solid tumors. However, its clinical application is limited because of cisplatin- induced nephrotoxicity. A known complication of cisplatin is acute kidney injury (AKI). Deletion polymorphisms of GSTM1 and GSTT1, members of the glutathione S-transferase family, are common in humans and are presumed to be associated with various kidney diseases.

pmc-11500340.title: Development of a colloidal gold immunochromatographic test strip for detecting the smooth Brucella
pmc-11500340.creator: Qi Wu, Xiaohan Guo, Qianhan Huang, Yujia Xie, Liping Guo, Xiangdong Yang, Mingjun Sun, Dehui Yin
pmc-11500340.description: Brucellosis, caused by Gram-negative Brucella, spreads in human and animal populations through contact with infected animals and products. Developing a rapid and sensitive detection technology for pathogen is crucial to reduce the risk of this disease transmitting between animal populations and to humans.

pmc-11710817.title: Clinical criteria for a limbic‐predominant amnestic neurodegenerative syndrome highly associated with TDP‐43 and slow clinical progression
pmc-11710817.creator: Nick Corriveau‐Lecavalier, Hugo Botha, Jonathan Graff‐Radford, Aaron Switzer, Scott A. Przybelski, Heather J. Wiste, Melissa E. Murray, Ross R. Reichard, Dennis W. Dickson, Aivi T. Nguyen, Vijay K. Ramanan, Stuart J. McCarter, Brad Boeve, Mary M. Machulda, Julie A. Fields, Nikki H. Stricker, Peter T
pmc-11710817.description: BackgroundLimbic‐predominant age‐related TDP‐43 encephalopathy (LATE) is a neuropathologically‐defined disease, and it is frequently comorbid with Alzheimer’s disease neuropathological change (ADNC). However, the neurological syndrome associated with LATE neuropathological change (LATE‐NC) is not defined. We propose a set of clinical criteria for a limbic‐predominant amnestic neurodegenerative syndrome (LANS) that is highly associated with LATE‐NC.

pmc-12593624.title: Real-life implementation of prenatal cell-free DNA screening with in vitro fetal enrichment virtually eliminates the need for redraws and improves performance: A cohort study
pmc-12593624.creator: Sylvie Giroux, Seyedeh Saideh Daryabari, André Caron, Julie Jeukens, Yves Giguère, Jean-Claude Forest, François Audibert, Emmanuel Bujold, Sylvie Langlois, François Rousseau
pmc-12593624.description: PurposeInsufficient fetal fraction is a significant cause of prenatal cell-free DNA (cfDNA) screening failure, affecting 2% to 5% of samples, particularly among women with high body mass index (BMI). We evaluated the clinical impacts of in vitro fetal enrichment in a public prenatal cfDNA screening laboratory, hypothesizing that it would lower failure rates.

pmc-12606010.title: Metabolomics and metagenomics in mice reveal the role of the gut microbiota in tryptophan metabolism
pmc-12606010.creator: Margaux Levé, Paolo Manghi, Marius Bredon, Antoine Lefevre, Serena Manara, Federica Armanini, Patrick Emond, Julien Planchais, Nathalie Rolhion, Nicola Segata, Harry Sokol
pmc-12606010.description: SummaryTryptophan metabolism plays a key role in host-microbiota interactions, producing a wide array of bioactive metabolites. However, our understanding of the interactions between tryptophan metabolites and the gut microbiota is still limited. Using targeted quantitative metabolomics and metagenomics in mice across various compartments, we showed that the cecal microbiota massively impacts tryptophan metabolism both in the gut and systemically.

pmc-13107008.title: Accurate Asthma-COPD Overlap Classification via Deep Transfer Learning in Medical Image Segmentation
pmc-13107008.creator: Weijie Ye, Dieyi Mo, Yubin Yang
pmc-13107008.description: Differentiating asthma from chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) remains challenging in clinical practice, and asthma-COPD overlap (ACO) lacks universally accepted diagnostic criteria. In this study, we propose a chest computed tomography (CT) image segmentation framework based on deep transfer learning to support imaging-assisted ACO-related classification as a proof-of-concept approach.

pmc-13384168.title: Current evidence on radiofrequency denervation for chronic low back pain: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13384168.creator: Kamilla My Thanh Lê Truong, Esther Maas, Mikkel Mylius Rasmussen, Raymond Ostelo, Heikki Hurri, Maurits W van Tulder
pmc-13384168.description: ObjectiveTo assess the effects of radiofrequency (RF) denervation for chronic low back pain (LBP) from facet joint, sacroiliac joint, discogenic and non-specific pain.DesignSystematic review and meta-analysis.Data sourcesWe searched Medline, Embase, Cochrane Library, CINAHL, PsycINFO, ClinicalTrials.gov and WHO ICTRP up to 18 February 2025 for randomised controlled trials (RCTs).
